rules.title: Pre-occupancy walk-through: your right, and deposit protection
rules.description: Per § 47a-7c, the landlord must offer the tenant the opportunity to do a pre-occupancy walk-through and complete a checklist of existing conditions. The landlord may not later keep any part of the deposit, or charge the tenant, for any condition noted on that checklist. This is a tenant protection, surfaced when the lease references move-in condition / inspections.
rules.tenant_explainer: Before you move in, you have the right to a documented walk-through with the landlord. Anything you note as already damaged can't be taken out of your deposit later — so ask for the walk-through and keep your copy.

citations.label: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7c
citations.quote: … prior to the tenant's occupancy of a dwelling unit, a landlord shall offer such tenant the opportunity to conduct a walk-through of the dwelling unit. … Upon the tenant's vacating of the dwelling unit, the landlord may not retain any part of the security deposit … or seek payment from the tenant for any condition, defect or damage that was noted in the preoccupancy walk-through checklist.
